title: What makes a racy frame racy?
text:
Tip




Hover over data for model and frame size identification.
Scroll legend and click on items to identify specific model and frame size combinations.
Click on popup icon-bar over legend to zoom in/out and pan.









Note



Classification of gravel bikes is based on a frame size that fits a 175 cm high rider (generally frame size M or 54), according to manufacturer’s charts.



Racy bike frames have a combination of low stack, short front-center, high head tube angles, and low trail




















Racy frames have short reach, relative to rowdy frames








Racy frames have short chainstays (and rear-center), relative to relaxed frames








Racy frames can have low seat tube angles








Racy frames tend to have short front and rear centers. Relaxed frames tend to have long front and rear centers. So both racy and relaxed frames have low front-center:rear-center but for different reasons.

p9







Stack:Reach and bottom brack drop aren’t really related to relaxedness

title: What makes a rowdy frame rowdy?
text:
Tip




Hover over data for model and frame size identification.
Scroll legend and click on items to identify specific model and frame size combinations.
Click on popup icon-bar over legend to zoom in/out and pan.









Note



Classification of gravel bikes is based on a frame size that fits a 175 cm high rider (generally frame size M or 54), according to manufacturer’s charts.



Rowdy frames have long front ends, slack headtube angles and high trail
























Stack, seattube angle, bottom bracket drop, and chainstay length aren’t really related to rowdiness

title: How does a suspension fork change bike geometry – Plots of data
text:
Tips for navigating




Hover over data for model and frame size identification.
Scroll legend and click on items to identify specific model.
Click on popup icon-bar over legend to zoom in/out and pan.









More notes!



More notes at the bottom!












Fork




rigid





30 mm





40 mm





50 mm














































Note



Classification of gravel bikes is based on a frame size that fits a 175 cm high rider (generally frame size M or 54), according to manufacturer’s charts.








Note



The suspension fork length and geometry is based on 20% sag: fork_length - 0.2*travel








A Rudy Fork geometry corrector



Rockshox recommends 5% sag (as opposed to 20% sag) on the Rudy fork. The geometry measures will be half-way between the target fork and the next-size up fork (for example, for a 30 mm Rudy fork, the geometry will be between the measures for the 30 mm fork and the 40 mm fork, of the same offset)








Gravel forks




Cane Creek Invert has two models: 30 mm (425 mm axle-crown) and 40 (435 mm axle-crown) mm travel. Both models have 45 mm offset
Rockshox Rudy has four models: 30 mm (425 mm axle-crown) and 40 (435 mm axle-crown) mm travel, each with either 45 mm or 51 mm offset.
Fox 32 TC Factory has four models: 40 (435.5 mm axle-crown) mm and 50 (445.5 mm axle-crown) mm travel, each with either 45 mm or 50 mm offset.
Lauf has one model with 30 mm travel (425 Axle Crown and 47 mm offset)

title: What makes a relaxed frame relaxed?
text:
Tip




Hover over data for model and frame size identification.
Scroll legend and click on items to identify specific model and frame size combinations.
Click on popup icon-bar over legend to zoom in/out and pan.









Note



Classification of gravel bikes is based on a frame size that fits a 175 cm high rider (generally frame size M or 54), according to manufacturer’s charts.



Relaxed bike frames have a combination of high stack, short reach, and long chain stays












By themselves, stack and reach aren’t really related to relaxedness












Headtube angle, seattube angle, bottom bracket drop, and trail aren’t really related to relaxedness

title: How does a suspension fork change bike geometry – Tables of data
text:
How to search for a specific model and size!




Use the pop-up box at the upper-left to search for a specific bike model and size.
If there is already a model in the pop-up box then


click in the box
hit the delete key
start typing model name.









Tip



More notes at the bottom!








Model




















Note



The suspension fork length and geometry is based on 20% sag: fork_length - 0.2*travel








A Rudy Fork geometry corrector



Rockshox recommends 5% sag on the Rudy fork while Fox, Cane Creek, and Lauf recommend (or are tuned for) 20% sag. The sus geometry for a rudy fork will be

For 30 mm fork, 20% sag is 419 mm AC and 5% sag is 423.5 mm AC. For a 40 mm fork, 20% sag is 427 mm AC. So the sus geometry of a Rudy fork will be 1/2way between the measures for the 30 mm and 40 mm forks here.
For 40 mm fork, 20% sag is 427 mm AC and 5% sag is 433 mm AC. For a 50 mm fork, 20% sag is 437 mm AC. So the sus geometry of a Rudy fork will be more than 1/2way between the measures for the 40 mm and 50 mm forks here.









HGravel forks




Cane Creek Invert has two models: 30 mm (425 mm axle-crown) and 40 (435 mm axle-crown) mm travel. Both models have 45 mm offset
Rockshox Rudy has four models: 30 mm (425 mm axle-crown) and 40 (435 mm axle-crown) mm travel, each with either 45 mm or 51 mm offset.
Fox 32 TC Factory has four models: 40 (435.5 mm axle-crown) mm and 50 (445.5 mm axle-crown) mm travel, each with either 45 mm or 50 mm offset.
Lauf has one model with 30 mm travel (425 Axle Crown and 47 mm offset)

title: Gravel Bike Geometry Project
text:
Start here
The Which bikes are racy/rowdy/relaxed? page contains the plot showing overall similarity among all gravel bike models in the database. Click on the points for finding bikes in the style you’re seeking. The plot also includes filters for finding bikes with specific features.











A little deeper
The What makes a rowdy frame rowdy? and What makes a relaxed frame relaxed? pages are full of plots showing which frame measures are most correlated with a style, and which aren’t.


Into the weeds
The Gravel 2D page contains interactive, 2D scatter plots of different pairs of frame geometry measures for all gravel bike models and frame sizes in the database.











A view from afar
The What is Gravel Style? page compares gravel bikes in the database to Road Race, Road Endurance, Cyclocross, and XC Mountain bikes.











The classification
The Gravel Tree page contains a tree diagram showing the relative similarity in frame geometry among all gravel bikes in the database and the clustering of the models into three major styles.









The Gravel Table page contains a table of the classification of all gravel bike models in the database into All-road, Endurance, and Trail categories.











Also, check out the Gravel Stories
Which gravel bikes have mountain bike inspired geometry?
Is a gravel bike a 1990s mountain bike?
